title: Rate limits on the sign-in mint and consume endpoints
description: POST /login and GET /login/verify are rate limited independently. The mint endpoint's ceiling is tight enough to make magic-link flooding unattractive and loose enough that a legitimate operator retry does not trip it; the blueprint defaults to five mints per minute per client key. The consume endpoint's ceiling defends against token-guessing sweeps; the blueprint defaults to twenty attempts per minute per client key. Both endpoints emit Retry-After with an honest wait window on 429 responses. Rate-limit rejections do not reveal registration state.
rationale: An unbounded mint endpoint is an email-bombing pipeline aimed at the operator's own inbox; an unbounded consume endpoint is a brute-force pipeline aimed at the token space. Class-appropriate limits with honest Retry-After close both without asking the operator to configure a WAF.
